nodes.title: Make cooking a shared thing
nodes.distillate_text: Reframe from 'me cooking cheaply' to 'a few of us cooking together' — unlocks bulk without a car each.
nodes.body: What if cooking cheaply isn't a solo chore but something a few neighbors do together?

nodes.title: Cook most dinners at home
nodes.distillate_text: Home dinners could halve the eating-out line — if I can keep it up on busy nights.
nodes.body: Eating out is the leak. What if most weeknights were home-cooked instead?

nodes.title: Cut my food spending by 30%
nodes.distillate_text: Eating out is the biggest leak; the fix is cooking more at home plus smarter shopping.
nodes.body: Where does the money actually go — groceries, eating out, or food that spoils?

nodes.title: A neighborhood supper club
nodes.distillate_text: A few homes bulk-buy together, batch-cook, and split meals — cheaper food and less cooking for everyone.
nodes.body: The fusion: pool the shopping, share the cooking, split the meals — cheaper and less work than going it alone.

nodes.title: No easy way to buy in bulk
nodes.distillate_text: Flipped: the missing bulk access isn't a wall — it's the reason to team up with others.
nodes.body:
The cheap bulk store is 40 minutes away and I have no car — bulk saving is real but I can't reach it alone.

**Flipped.** Who else near me wants bulk groceries? What does sharing the trip unlock?

nodes.title: A shared bulk pantry
nodes.distillate_text: A small shared pantry lets a few homes buy in bulk and draw down as they need it.
nodes.body: Bulk only works if there's somewhere to keep it. A shared pantry solves storage for everyone.

nodes.title: Trade dishes you're good at
nodes.body: Everyone can cook one thing well. Trade a portion of your specialty for someone else's. Just a spark for now.

nodes.title: Shop with a list, buy staples in bulk
nodes.distillate_text: A fixed list kills impulse buys; bulk staples cut unit cost — needs discipline.
nodes.body: Impulse buys and small packs quietly add up. A list plus bulk staples fixes both.

nodes.title: Cook double, split with a neighbor
nodes.distillate_text: One big cook feeds two homes for barely more effort — halves both cost and cooking time.
nodes.body: If I'm already batch-cooking, cooking double and splitting is almost free.

nodes.title: Sunday batch-cook + a fixed grocery list
nodes.distillate_text: Batch-cook on Sundays and shop one strict list — clears the 30%, if I can buy in bulk.
nodes.body: Combine the two: cook once on Sunday, shop one disciplined list. What is still in the way?

facets.name: cost
facets.distillate: A group hits bulk pricing no one could alone — the same saving as the bulk store.

facets.name: access
facets.distillate: Someone has to organize the trip and the rota — the thing that makes or breaks it.

facets.name: cost
facets.distillate: Eating out is ~40% of the total — the number every option is judged against.

facets.name: time
facets.distillate: Only ~4 hours a week to cook — the real constraint.

facets.name: effort
facets.distillate: One person cooks once instead of two people cooking twice.
